_comment: Deterministic collateral cases (issue #5, docs/pre_build_checklist.md §6). Provenance: constructed. All money values are PreciseNumber-style attoTIG decimal strings (accounting.md §3); every derived amount was computed by hand with integer math only. P, X, J[k], and fees are fixture policy inventions, NOT settled protocol constants (mining_system.md §11 leaves the numerical values of X and J[k] open). Per-track fees F[s,t] are supplied as inputs, never derived, so no precommit-fee formula assumption is embedded (see README open questions). Expected values are recorded independently of any implementation; each names the rule that derives it.

conventions.money_unit: attoTIG decimal string (1 TIG = 10^18 attoTIG), accounting.md §3
conventions.policy_version: policy_v1_fixture — a fixture invention, versioned per architecture.md §7.6

fixture_policy.note: P = live config.reports.penalty_amount at decision snapshot s (accounting.md §11.4). X = versioned per-failure charge, numerical value intentionally open (mining_system.md §11).

cases.name: per_track_bundle_counts_max_reserve
cases.description: One proposed benchmark with two possible tracks and different per-track bundle counts. The precommit reserve is the maximum assignment reserve across all proposed tracks because TIG selects the track only after precommit.
cases.action_or_event: Decision engine proposes bundle counts for all tracks; Controller computes the reservation before any precommit.

expected.derivation: method_reserve = P*B: 10 TIG*4 = 40 TIG; 10 TIG*10 = 100 TIG. assignment_reserve = method_reserve + F + X: 40 + 0.09 + 2 = 42.09 TIG; 100 + 0.11 + 2 = 102.11 TIG. precommit_reserve = max = 102.11 TIG.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (method_reserve[s,t] = P[s]*B[t]; assignment_reserve[s,t] = method_reserve + F[s,t] + X[policy]; precommit_reserve = max over proposed tracks); mining_system.md §6.1 (reserve at least the maximum live method-penalty and per-failure exposure across proposed tracks; the maximum is required because TIG selects the track only after precommit)

cases.name: reservation_reduced_after_track_confirmed_never_increased
cases.description: After TIG confirms the selected track and exact fee_paid, the open reservation may be reduced to that track's exact requirement. It is never increased.
cases.action_or_event: TIG confirms the precommit with selected track t001 and exact fee_paid.

expected.derivation: Exact requirement for the confirmed track: P*B + fee_paid + X = 40 + 0.09 + 2 = 42.09 TIG. Reduction from 102.11 TIG is permitted; any increase (e.g. by applying a later pool policy) is forbidden.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (once TIG confirms the selected track and exact fee_paid, the reservation may be reduced to that track's exact requirement, never increased by silently applying a later pool policy)

cases.name: simultaneous_reservations_second_admitted
cases.description: A second benchmark for the same member is admitted while the first reservation is still open, because unreserved eligible collateral still covers the new precommit reserve.
cases.action_or_event: Controller runs the admission check for a second precommit intent while bench_b10 is still unresolved.

expected.derivation: eligible_collateral - reserved_exposure = 250 - 102.11 = 147.89 TIG >= precommit_reserve 102.11 TIG, so admission passes; reserved_exposure becomes 204.22 TIG. Each reservation is attached to its own benchmark.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (new work is allowed only if eligible_collateral[m] - reserved_exposure[m] >= precommit_reserve; reserved_exposure = sum of open assignment reservations); mining_system.md §6.1 (the reservation is specific to that member and benchmark and cannot collateralize another unresolved benchmark)

cases.name: simultaneous_reservations_third_denied
cases.description: A third simultaneous reservation is denied: the two open reservations may not be reused as collateral, and the unreserved remainder is below the new precommit reserve.
cases.action_or_event: Controller runs the admission check for a third precommit intent while bench_b10 and bench_b11 are both unresolved.

expected.derivation: 250 - 204.22 = 45.78 TIG < 102.11 TIG, so the check fails. No reservation is created and no precommit intent exists. Existing reservations are unchanged.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (admission inequality; one reservation never collateralizes several simultaneous risks); mining_system.md §6.1

cases.name: insufficient_balance_after_pending_return_and_freeze
cases.description: Eligible collateral subtracts pending returns and frozen charge/slash amounts before the admission check; the raw finalized deposit alone would have passed.
cases.action_or_event: Controller runs the admission check for a first precommit intent.

expected.derivation: eligible_collateral = 120 - 10 - 15 = 95 TIG. 95 - 0 = 95 TIG < precommit_reserve 102.11 TIG, so admission fails even though the raw finalized deposit (120 TIG) exceeds the reserve.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (eligible_collateral[m] = finalized security-deposit liability - pending returns - frozen charge/slash amounts; admission inequality)

cases.name: new_tier_fee_does_not_bypass_collateral_gate
cases.description: A removed member rejoins by paying J[k] again; the fee debit reduces the deposit, the pre-removal reservation persists, and the ordinary collateral gate still denies new work.

open_reservations.note: created before tier removal; not cleared by removal or repurchase

cases.action_or_event: Member pays J[2] again immediately after removal, then requests new work.

expected.derivation: Fee debit: 50 - 5 = 45 TIG finalized. 45 - 42.09 (open reservation, unaffected by removal/rejoin) = 2.91 TIG < 42.09 TIG, so admission fails. The newly paid joining fee changes nothing in the collateral gate.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.6 (a newly paid tier fee never bypasses that gate) and §11.3 (rejoining does not release or reset outstanding reservations); mining_system.md §6.1 (a deposit or newly paid joining fee does not erase an outstanding liability) and §10 invariant 24

cases.name: live_penalty_change_pauses_new_precommits
cases.description: penalty_amount changes on the newly accepted block; new precommits pause until compatibility review, while the already-open reservation keeps its recorded value.
cases.action_or_event: Pool reads penalty_amount at accepted block 100091 and observes it changed from 10 TIG to 12 TIG.

expected.new_precommits: paused until compatibility has been reviewed and requirements recomputed
expected.derivation: The change alone pauses admission of new precommits. The open reservation is not recomputed: its amount and recorded P/policy version are unchanged by the live change.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.5 (the pool reads penalty_amount every accepted block, records the exact value and policy used by each reservation, and any change immediately pauses new precommits until compatibility has been reviewed and requirements recomputed)

cases.name: penalty_change_mid_flight_no_retroactive_increase
cases.description: After review resumes precommits at the new penalty, the mid-flight benchmark's reservation is still settled at its own assignment-snapshot values; only new decisions use the new P.
cases.action_or_event: TIG confirms bench_b30's track after the penalty change; the pool separately admits a new benchmark under the reviewed P = 12 TIG.

expected.derivation: bench_b30 reduces to its assignment-snapshot exact requirement 10*4 + 0.09 + 2 = 42.09 TIG; applying the later P = 12 TIG to it is forbidden. The new benchmark's reserve uses the new snapshot: 12*4 + 0.09 + 2 = 50.09 TIG. Whether TIG itself can apply a later penalty retroactively to an open benchmark is an open spike question (see README) — this case asserts only pool-side reservation behavior.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (never increased by silently applying a later pool policy) and §11.5 (retroactivity of TIG report penalties is an explicit pre-mainnet spike question; residual risk is handled by a configured buffer, not by retroactively enlarging the member's reservation)

cases.name: reservation_release_split_X_vs_method
cases.description: On TIG verification without a chargeable tier failure the X portion of the reservation releases, while the method portion stays reserved until the benchmark can no longer generate a method-verification penalty and every report/arbitration is terminal.
cases.action_or_event: TIG records bench_b40 as verified; no chargeable tier failure is attributed to the member.

expected.method_release_condition: benchmark can no longer generate a method-verification penalty and every report/arbitration is terminal
expected.derivation: The X portion (2 TIG) releases on verification without a chargeable failure. The method portion (40 TIG) remains reserved because reports are not yet terminal.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.4 (the method portion remains reserved until the benchmark can no longer generate a method-verification penalty and every report/arbitration is terminal; the X portion releases when TIG verifies the benchmark without a chargeable tier failure)
